__
 
• **Redox reactions **include a **change in the oxidation state** of the substrate.
 
• **Loss of electrons** or a** rise in the oxidation state **are both examples of** oxidation.**
 
• **Gaining electrons **or** lowering the oxidation state **are both considered to be **reductions.**
 
• In the reaction, CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, **Cu is reduced** whereas **Hydrogen is oxidized.**
 
• Redox reactions fall into one of **two categories:**
 
• **Electron-transfer:**
 
 
• Only one electron (typically) moves from the **reducing agent to the oxidant **during an electron transfer.
 
• It is common to talk about this kind of redox reaction in terms of** redox couples and electrode potentials.**
 
 
 
• **Atom transfer:**
 
 
• A transfer of an atom occurs when **one substrate gives way to another.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

• A molecule, atom, or ion undergoes oxidation when it** loses electrons **as a result of a process.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition:**
 
 
• The process of **recycling nutrients** that have been **consumed by an organism** (plant or animal) to create its body begins with decomposition.
 
 
 
• **Reduction:**
 
 
• Reduction is the term used to **describe a reaction** in which a **reactant picks up electrons.**

questions.question: If the number x3331 is divisible by 11, what is the face value of x?
questions.solution:
Given:

x3331

Concept used:

If the difference of the sum of alternative digits of a number is divisible by 11, then that number is divisible by 11 completely.

Calculation:

Difference between the sum of the digits at alternate places of x3331

⇒ (x + 3 + 1) - (3 + 3)

⇒ x + 4 - 6

⇒ x - 2

Now, x can only be 2 which makes (x - 2) = 0 which is divisible by 11. (∵ x can be any integer starting from 1 to 9)

So, x = 2

**∴ The face value of x is 2.**

questions.question: Some one rupee, 50 paisa and 25 paisa coins make up rupees 93.75 and their numbers are in the proportion of 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 5. Find the number of each type of coins?

Let the number of coins of one rupee, 50 paisa and 25 paise be 3x, 4x and 5x respectively.

3x × 1 + 4x × 0.50 + 5x × 0.25 = 93.75

⇒ 3x + 2x + 1.25x = 93.75

⇒ 6.25x = 93.75

⇒ x = 93.75/6.25

⇒ x = 15

Hence, there are (3 × 15) i.e. 45 one rupee coins, (4 × 15) i.e. 60, 50 paisa coins, and (5 × 15) i.e. 75, 25 paise coins.

**∴ There are 45, 60, and 75 coins of one rupee, 50 paisa, and 25 paisa respectively.**

questions.question: One of the two inlet pipes works twice as efficiently as the other. The two, working alongside a drain pipe that can empty a cistern all by itself in 8 hours, can fill the empty cistern in 8 hours. How many hours will the less efficient inlet pipe take to fill the empty cistern by itself?
questions.solution:
Given:

One of the two inlet pipes works twice as efficiently as the other. 

The two, working alongside a drain pipe that can empty a cistern all by itself in 8 hours, can fill the empty cistern in 8 hours.

Concept used:

If two workers take X and Y hours respectively to complete a task independently, then time taken to complete the work together = frac {XY}{X + Y} hours

Calculation:

Let the time taken by the more efficient inlet pipe be Q hours.

So, time taken by the less efficient inlet pipe = 2Q hours

​According to the concept,

Time taken to fill the cistern if only two inlet pipes are open together

⇒ frac {2Q times Q}{2Q + Q} = {frac {2Q}{3}} hours

Time taken to fill the cistern if two inlet pipes are open together alongside the drain pipe

⇒ frac {{frac {2Q}{3}} times {-8}}{{frac {2Q}{3}} - 8} (A negative sign is taken since the drain pipe empties the cistern)

⇒ frac {-16Q}{2Q - 24} hours

​According to the question,

frac {-16Q}{2Q - 24} = 8

⇒ frac {-2Q}{2Q - 24} = 1

⇒ 2Q - 24 = -2Q

⇒ 4Q = 24

⇒ Q = 6

⇒ 2Q = 12

Now, time taken by the less efficient pipe to fill the cistern = 12 hours

**∴ The less efficient inlet pipe takes 12 hours to fill the empty cistern by itself.**

questions.question: Two pipes fill a tank when working individually in 25 and 40 hours, respectively while a third pipe can drain the filled tank in 16 hours. If all the three pipes are turned on at the same time when the tank is empty, how long will it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM (25, 40, 16) = 400 units.

Individual efficiencies: A = 16, B = 10, C = −25 units/hr.

Net efficiency (A+B+C) = 16 + 10 − 25 = 1 unit/hr.

Time required = 400 ÷ 1 = 400 hours.

400 hours = (384 + 16) hours = 16 days 16 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days 16 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A = 25 hours

Time taken by Pipe B = 40 hours

Time taken by Pipe C (outlet) = 16 hours

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Pipes

 Efficiency
 
 

 Pipe A

 Pipe B

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity = LCM (25, 40, 16) = 400 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of (A + B + C) = 16 + 10 − 25 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Total time taken = 400 ÷ 1 = 400 hours

⇒ To convert hours into days: 400 ÷ 24 = 16 days and 16 hours (since 24 × 16 = 384)

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days 16 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Work in Pipes

An outlet pipe (leak) performs negative work. While calculating combined efficiency, subtract the rate of the outlet pipe from the rate of the inlet pipes.

LCM Method

Total capacity is assumed as the LCM of individual times taken. Individual efficiency = Total capacity ÷ Individual time.

Time Conversion

questions.question: Find the length of one side of a rhombus whose area is 24 cm² and the sum of the lengths of its diagonals is 14 cm.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let diagonals be d₁ and d₂.

Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂ = 24 ⇒ d₁ × d₂ = 48.

Given d₁ + d₂ = 14. By inspection, d₁ = 8 cm and d₂ = 6 cm.

Diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at 90°.

Side = √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the rhombus = 24 cm²

Sum of diagonals (d₁ + d₂) = 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of rhombus = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂

Relation between side (a) and diagonals: 4a² = d₁² + d₂²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38d299016e8aaa7dc46c97cc837203c679baf763563a5c28b7646391058fcec4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂ = 24

⇒ d₁ × d₂ = 48

⇒ We know the algebraic identity, (d₁ + d₂)² = d₁² + d₂² + 2d₁d₂

⇒ (14)² = d₁² + d₂² + 2 × 48

⇒ 196 = d₁² + d₂² + 96

⇒ d₁² + d₂² = 196 − 96 = 100

⇒ From the side-diagonal relation: 4a² = 100

⇒ a² = 25

⇒ a = 5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

All four sides of a rhombus are equal in length, and its opposite angles are equal.

Diagonals of a Rhombus

The diagonals bisect each other perpendicularly (at 90°) creating four congruent right-angled triangles.

Perimeter

The perimeter of a rhombus is given by 4 × a, where 'a' is the length of one side.
</p
